Introduce yourself. Name, degree and university, final-year project in one line, PEC registration, any site or design experience, and why this department. Keep it under one minute. Why do you want to join this department? Link it to public service and the department's work: e.g., C&W builds and maintains provincial roads and buildings; Irrigation runs canals, barrages and drainage; PHE gives safe water and sanitation. Mention a current project of the department if you know one. What are the duties of an SDO / AE? Run a sub-division: supervise works and contractors, check measurements in the MB, test materials, prepare estimates and bills, maintain records and stores, handle complaints, and report to the XEN. Hierarchy of a works department? Chief Engineer → Superintending Engineer (circle) → Executive Engineer (division) → SDO/AE (sub-division) → Sub-Engineer → work-charged staff. Why register with PEC? Under the PEC Act 1976 only registered engineers may practise or hold engineering posts; PE status needs 5 years after RE, CPD points and the EPE exam. Your final-year project — what did you learn? State the problem, your method, one result with a number, and one limitation you would fix now.

How do you check concrete quality on site? Approve materials and mix design; check slump each batch; cast 6 cylinders/cubes per pour (or per ACI frequency); check cover, formwork and vibration; cure for at least 7 days (OPC); review 7- and 28-day results. Slump test values? Pavements 25–50 mm, beams/columns 75–100 mm, heavily reinforced or pumped 100–150 mm. Shear slump means the mix is lean or harsh — redo. Cube results are low — what will you do? Check testing and curing records first; then take cores (ACI: average of 3 cores ≥ 0.85 f′c and none < 0.75 f′c is acceptable); if still low, load test or strengthen, and recover the cost from the contractor as per the contract. How do you check a brick on site? Size and shape, uniform colour, metallic ring when struck, no lumps of lime; 24-h water absorption ≤ 20% for first class; no efflorescence; compressive strength by test. How do you check steel reinforcement? Mill certificate, grade marks, diameter and weight per metre (d²/162 kg/m), bend test, tensile test from each lot; check bar spacing, laps, cover and chairs before the pour. Minimum cover? ACI 318 cast-in-place: slabs 20 mm, beams/columns 40 mm, footings against earth 75 mm. Curing period and methods? OPC at least 7 days, blended cements 10–14 days; ponding, wet hessian, sprinkling, curing compound, plastic sheets. When can formwork be removed? Vertical faces 16–24 h; slab soffits with props left 3–7 days; removing props 7–14 days for slabs and 14–21 days for beams (OPC

What is the Measurement Book? The basic record of quantities of work done and supplied, written by the measuring officer at site; every payment is based on it. Entries are in ink, never erased, and checked by the SDO/XEN. Administrative approval vs technical sanction? A/A — the administrative department accepts the need and the cost of the work; T/S — the competent engineer approves the detailed estimate and design. No work starts without both and funds. When is a revised estimate needed? When the sanctioned estimate is likely to be exceeded by more than 5% (or the scope changes materially). What is a running bill and a final bill? Running (interim) bills pay for work done to date on measurement, less retention and advances; the final bill closes the account after completion and final measurements. Security deposit / retention money? A percentage held from each bill (commonly 5–10%) and released after the defects liability period. Mobilisation and secured advance? Mobilisation advance — paid at start against a bank guarantee, recovered from bills. Secured advance — paid against materials brought to site (usually up to 75% of their value), recovered when used. How do you calculate quantity of brickwork? Volume in m³ (or 100 cft) less openings above the deduction limit; ≈ 390–400 Pakistani 9 × 4½ × 3 in bricks per m³ with 10 mm joints (≈ 500 modular bricks), plus ≈ 5% wastage; field rule 13.5 bricks per cft. Cement for 1 m³ of 1:2:4 concrete? Dry volume 1.54 m³ → cement = 1.54/

Main stages of public procurement? Need and estimate → bidding documents → advertisement (PPRA website) → bid opening → evaluation → award → contract signing → performance guarantee → execution. Single-stage one-envelope vs two-envelope? One envelope: technical and price together, lowest evaluated responsive bid wins (normal works). Two envelope: technical opened first, price only of qualified bidders (complex works). Bid security and performance security? Bid security ≤ 5% of estimated cost (PPRA rules) to keep bids serious; performance security (often 5–10%) from the winner as guarantee of completion. What are liquidated damages? A pre-agreed amount per day of delay, deducted from bills if the contractor fails to finish on time — usually capped at a percentage of the contract price. What is a variation order? Written instruction changing the scope, quantity or specification; priced by contract rates, rates for similar items, or new rates agreed per the contract. What is FIDIC? International standard conditions of contract; PEC's Standard Form of Bidding Documents for civil works are based on them. Item-rate vs lump-sum vs percentage-rate contract? Item rate: paid per measured quantity at quoted rates (most common). Lump sum: fixed price for defined work. Percentage rate: bidder quotes ± % on the schedule of rates.

Explain one-way and two-way slabs. Long/short span ratio > 2 → one-way (bends in one direction); ≤ 2 → two-way. One-way slab main steel along the short span. Why is a beam under-reinforced? Steel yields before concrete crushes, so it fails with large deflection and warning (ductile). ACI keeps net tensile strain ≥ 0.005 for tension-controlled sections. Minimum and maximum steel in columns? 1% to 8% of gross area (ACI); at least 4 bars in rectangular and 6 in circular columns. What load factors do you use? ACI 318 / ASCE 7: 1.4D, and 1.2D + 1.6L for gravity; combinations with wind and earthquake as per ASCE 7. What is the effective length of a column? Length between points of zero moment: K = 0.5 fixed–fixed, 0.7 fixed–pinned, 1.0 pinned–pinned, 2.0 cantilever. How do you choose a foundation? From soil investigation (SPT, bearing capacity, water table), loads and settlement limits: isolated footings for good soil, combined/strap where footings are close or near a boundary, raft for weak soil or heavy loads, piles where good stratum is deep. What causes cracks in buildings? Shrinkage, thermal movement, settlement, overloading, corrosion of steel, poor curing, earthquake. Find the cause before repair; monitor with tell-tales. Which seismic zone is your city in? Give the BCP 2007 zone (e.g., Lahore 2A, Islamabad 2B, Quetta 4) and say BCP 2021 now uses IBC-type seismic design categories.

Layers of a flexible pavement? Subgrade → subbase → base → asphalt base → wearing course; load spreads through layers. Rigid pavement carries load by slab bending. Why do roads fail early? Poor drainage, overloading of trucks, weak subgrade, poor compaction, wrong bitumen grade or content, and lack of maintenance. What is camber and its value? Cross slope for drainage: ≈ 1.7–2.5% for bituminous roads (more in heavy rainfall), 2.5–3% for WBM/gravel, 3–4% for earth roads. Marshall test — what does it give? Stability (load at failure) and flow (deformation) of a compacted asphalt specimen at 60 °C; used with density and voids to choose the optimum bitumen content. What is a prime coat and a tack coat? Prime coat — low-viscosity bitumen on an unbound granular base to bind and seal it. Tack coat — thin bitumen on an existing bound surface to bond the next layer. How will you improve drainage of a hill road? Side drains, catch-water drains above the cut, culverts at every stream, breast walls with weep holes, and proper camber.

Steps of conventional water treatment? Screening → aeration (if needed) → coagulation/flocculation → sedimentation → rapid sand filtration → disinfection (chlorine) → storage and distribution. How do you know water is safe? No E. coli in 100 mL, turbidity < 5 NTU, arsenic ≤ 0.05 mg/L (NSDWQ), and residual chlorine 0.2–0.5 mg/L at the tap. Per-capita demand you will use? Typical design values in Pakistan: ≈ 150–200 L/capita/day for urban areas and ≈ 45–100 L/capita/day for rural schemes (follow the department's design criteria). Difference between BOD and COD? BOD — oxygen used by bacteria to oxidise organic matter in 5 days at 20 °C; COD — oxygen needed to oxidise everything chemically. COD > BOD; BOD/COD ≈ 0.4–0.6 for domestic sewage. Minimum velocity in a sewer? Self-cleansing ≈ 0.6–0.75 m/s; maximum ≈ 2.5–3 m/s to avoid erosion. When is an EIA needed? For Schedule II projects under PEPA 1997 / provincial acts (large dams, highways, treatment plants, industry); smaller projects need an IEE.

Parts of a barrage? Weir with gates, divide wall, fish ladder, head regulators, guide banks, marginal bunds, silt excluder, downstream stilling basin and launching aprons. Weir vs barrage? A weir raises water mainly by its crest (few or no gates); a barrage controls the pond level mainly by gates across the river. What is Lacey's regime theory? Alluvial channels reach a stable "regime" section for a given discharge and silt factor; P = 4.75√Q, f = 1.76√d (d in mm). Duty and delta? Duty — area irrigated per cumec; delta — total depth of water a crop needs. Δ (m) = 8.64 B/D (B = base period in days, D in ha/cumec). Waterlogging — causes and cures? Seepage from canals, over-irrigation, poor drainage, high water table. Cures: canal lining, drains, tubewells (SCARP), controlled irrigation. Major dams of Pakistan? Tarbela (Indus, largest earth-fill), Mangla (Jhelum), under construction Diamer-Bhasha and Mohmand; Dasu hydropower on the Indus.

A contractor offers you money to pass poor work. What will you do? Refuse, record the defect in writing, order rectification as per contract, and report the attempt to the XEN — PEC code of ethics and government rules forbid it. Your senior asks you to sign a measurement you did not check. Politely decline to sign until you measure it yourself; the MB entry is your personal responsibility. A building under your supervision shows cracks after a storm. Make it safe (prop, vacate if needed), record and photograph, find the cause (settlement, overloading, poor work), get the design checked, then repair. Funds are short and the work must continue. Prioritise safety-critical and partly-finished items, report to the XEN with a revised programme, and do not make commitments beyond the funds released. Local people object to the project route. Listen and record objections, explain benefits and compensation, involve the district administration, and refer genuine design changes to the competent authority.
